commits.message: docs(protocol): the glyph header names the one table that pins the clip (brandon-unfiled-3248.1izo)

test(protocol): the glyph clip is pinned by the one table both runtimes assert (brandon-unfiled-3248.1izo)

What the clip does to a string is behaviour, and either runtime could change it, update its own hand-mirrored test, and leave the other unaware. The shared fixture now carries clip cases, so a clip rule changed in one runtime fails the other's test. The Rust clip takes its budget as a parameter so those cases can drive it.

The mirrored tests were also the only proof a message reaches the clip, so each runtime keeps one test that every message-bearing cause clips at the budget, with the expected text derived from the clip itself.
fix(carousel): names are the leading literals, trial controls say trials, and a removed themeSwitcher points somewhere (brandon-menus-sjhy.vxr)

feat(carousel): the standard control names the setting it changes, not its value (brandon-menus-sjhy.vxr)

{{ carousel "apply" "open" "label" }} draws ◀ label ▶. The label is required, the neighbour ring and the themeSwitcher segment are gone, and a value outside the domain counts as the first member.

test(daemon): a real daemon starts only from a named process tier (candybar-testing-0x6u.886) (#525)

* test(daemon): every daemon a run starts is recorded and judged at its end (candybar-testing-0x6u.886)

* test(daemon): a test of the process is named for it, and everything else needs no build (candybar-testing-0x6u.886)

* test(daemon): a run's daemon starts are pinned at what a full run measures (candybar-testing-0x6u.886)

* test(daemon): CI runs the tier after the build and the rest before it, and preloads share one merge (candybar-testing-0x6u.886)

A run outside the tier needing no build was checked once by hand. CI now
partitions the suite at the build, so that holds on every push at no added
time. The ledger's NODE_OPTIONS merge was a copy of the stamp's, which that
file says there is one of. The pool case's cleanup no longer depends on the
third spawn having succeeded.

* test(daemon): a dying process's stderr is read once its pipe closes, and the tier has one spelling (candybar-testing-0x6u.886)

A readiness failure read the tail at the exit, which can land before the
pipe's last bytes, so the process that dies before its log opens could say
nothing. The tail is now a value that exists once the pipe has closed.
`pnpm test:process` reads the tier's pattern from its one home, so CI no
longer spells it.
